An electromagnetic plane wave: E and B are the same at every point of a yz plane

Animation of an electromagnetic plane wave. Oblique three-dimensional view with the x axis to the right, y up and z towards the viewer. Three grey translucent rectangles lie in yz planes at fixed positions x_1, x_1 + lambda/2 and x_1 + lambda along the x axis. On each, at nine points arranged three by three, a magenta electric-field vector E points along y and a blue magnetic-field vector B along z. Within one plane all nine pairs are identical and grow, shrink and reverse together as the wave passes; the middle plane is always opposite to the outer two, which are in step with each other. Faint magenta and blue sinusoids along the x axis show the wave profile E(x, t) and B(x, t) sliding to the right at speed c, and the vectors on each plane match the curves where that plane sits. A readout gives cos(kx - wt) on the three planes and a caption notes that the fields are the same at every point in a yz plane and that E, B and the direction of travel are mutually perpendicular.
